items.root_cause: A commodity registration and the recipe vocabulary that names the same food are two records written by two tools on two days, and nothing compares them when either lands. run-gates runs audit-ingredient-identity only as -SelfTest; its data pass runs once a day inside check-ad-cycles; apply-coverage-batch.ps1, new-commodity.ps1 and add-commodity-rule.ps1 never read db/ingredients.json. So 4880ebc98 could land three commodities that claim three vocabulary names, the rebid was deferred to another queue id (9b0825), and the next chain paged the gap as three NEW findings. Measured over the 61 commodities.json commits of the last 30 days: 10 vocabulary rows changed route in 6 commits, 4 of them newly off their bid (4880ebc98 x3, 828d5226b 'Cooked White Rice' rice -> unrouted). The split in this item is exactly such a change (Pepperoncini moves banana-peppers -> pepperoncini), which is why its rebid must ride the same push.

items.verdict_for_the_day: RESUME of the item plan-2026-09-22-11 closed deviated. The standing list (149 -> 91 today) is the output of a check that asks about ONE store per line on ONE of the three pricing surfaces, so it both misses what the reader sees and over-reports spellings. This item is the detection root fix for the whole family; the price fixes ride in 2026-09-26-177835 and the ruling half in 2026-09-25-f9c8ce.
evidence: Check (c) today tests only the costed basis store (Walmart first): 80 UNION-ROW lines over 14 (item, bid, product) pairs, 77 recipes, 72 not held (scratch re-derivation of the audit over the same inputs; per-pair rows in the routing artifact).

It silently skips 946 of 7,616 board-basis costed lines (744 board:<id>:recipeboard-* and 202 board:<id>:nomem:* whose store key never matches the comparison index) and never reads the 234 feed:<id> lines, which price through grocery/recipe-floor-id-map.json aliases (31 entries, e.g. rotini-pasta -> pasta, pineapple-chunks -> canned-pineapple, marinara-sauce -> pasta-sauce, pepperoncini -> banana-peppers).

What the reader sees: the recipe card and compute-v2 cheapest_ps take the minimum whole-package cost across EVERY store cell (package-cost-lib Get-PkgCheapestAcross). Simulated over all 587 specs against grocery/out/smp-feed.json pricing_inputs: 3,788 priced lines, of which 119 lines in 114 recipes (110 not held) are won by a store whose product does not name the ingredient, a different set from check (c)'s: e.g. Pasta Shells won at Aldi by 'Reggano Spaghetti' (8) and at Family Fare by 'Our Family Spaghetti 16 Oz' (5); Beef Flank/Sirloin Steak won at Family Fare by 'Fresh Usda Choice Whole Sirloin Tip' (25); Zucchini won at Walmart only 4 times, not 18.

Every store cell of every (item, priced id) pair used by a costed line: 102 board cells over 38 pairs plus 15 alias cells fail the head-word test today. Most are one food with two names ('Aldi Garbanzo Beans 15.5 OZ' for Chickpeas, 'Whole Boneless Pork Butt Roast Per LB' for Pork Shoulder, 'Happy Farms Neufchatel Cheese 8 OZ' for 1/3 Fat Cream Cheese, 'That's Smart! canola oil' for Vegetable Oil, 151 lines); some are real wrong foods the standing list never showed ('Wheat Thins Sundried Tomato & Basil Snacks 8.5 Oz' $3.99 in sun-dried-tomatoes at Family Fare).
The key is per costed line today (union|slug|item|id) and carries no product, so a standing key hides the NEXT wrong product at the same cell.

items.root_cause: The recipe price is bound to a commodity ID, and all three pricing surfaces (engine/cost-recipes Walmart-first, compute-v2 cheapest_ps and the card's costAt, both minimum across every store cell) price by that id with no notion of which food the line names. The only thing that asks whether the product is the ingredient is audit-ingredient-identity check (c), and it reads one store per line on one surface, skips the recipe-board and nomem lines, never reads the alias-priced lines, and keys findings without the product. So a union cell can price a line with another food at any store the card picks, and the list both misses it and fills with spellings nobody reviewed.

Of them, the defect half (Zucchini 18, Pepperoncini 3, Korean glass noodles 3, Blackened 1, Egg Yolk 1, Fresh Red Chili 1 = 27 lines) is planned in 2026-09-26-177835. What remains is one question about FORM and STYLE: not-held recipes carrying at least one such line: pasta shape 42 lines / 42 recipes (Pasta Shells 13, Spaghetti 10, Ziti 8, Orzo 4, Fettuccine 2 priced by 'Great Value Penne, 32 oz', Rotini 5 through the rotini-pasta -> pasta alias, priced by 'Reggano Spaghetti' at Aldi); pineapple chunks by crushed 4; cheese tortellini by tortelloni 3; marinara by pasta sauce 21 (alias marinara-sauce -> pasta-sauce, plus Rao's Marinara for Traditional Pasta Sauce); enchilada sauce by 'Las Palmas Medium Red Chile Sauce, 28 oz' 9; chili crisp by 'Lao Gan Ma Fried Chili Oil, 7.41 oz' 2; cajun by 'Tony Chachere's Creole Seasoning' at Fareway 13; green chile sauce by salsa verde 1. 88 distinct not-held recipes of 570.
items.root_cause: Board commodities are defined for the shopper's cheapest-of-a-class question ('Pasta (dry)', 'Canned Pineapple', 'Cajun / Creole Seasoning'), and whether a different form or style of the same food is the same food for a RECIPE line has never been ruled: the 2026-09-06 form rule (T2: weight or volume unit, format irrelevant) covers board cells, and the 2026-09-22 no-substitute ruling covers different foods.
items.resolution_note: Needs Brad: Q-2026-09-26-form-style (supersedes Q-2026-09-25-pasta-shape). The defect half of this residual (zucchini, pepperoncini, glass noodles, blackened, egg yolk, red chili) shipped under 2026-09-26-177835 and the detection fix under 2026-09-22-5a9676. On an answer: A records identity_same_as per pair (no price moves); B registers member commodities the way zucchini and pepperoncini were split and holds any recipe whose form is carried nowhere in Omaha.

open_questions_for_brad.question: Under your 2026-09-22 ruling (no ingredient priced as a different food), is a different FORM or STYLE of the same food the same food for a recipe line? Measured 2026-09-26: 88 of 570 not-held recipes carry at least one such line. FORM: pasta shape (42 recipes: shells, spaghetti, ziti, orzo, fettuccine and rotini priced by penne or spaghetti), pineapple chunks priced by crushed (4), cheese tortellini by tortelloni (3). STYLE: marinara priced by plain pasta sauce (21), enchilada sauce by Las Palmas Red Chile Sauce (9), cajun seasoning by Tony Chachere's Creole at Fareway (13), chili crisp by Lao Gan Ma Fried Chili Oil (2), green chile sauce by salsa verde (1).
options: A (recommended for FORM): extend your 2026-09-06 form rule T2 to recipes: when the unit is weight or volume, a different shape or cut is the same food. Each pair gets a reviewed same-food record; no price moves, nothing is held. Consequence: a shells recipe keeps pricing from the cheapest dry pasta, which may be spaghetti.

B (recommended for STYLE): a different style is a different food. Each style gets its own commodity the way zucchini and pepperoncini were split today, and a recipe whose style is carried nowhere in Omaha is held. Consequence: up to 46 recipes reprice from their own style's cells, and any whose style has no Omaha capture comes down until one lands.
C: B for everything, forms included. Consequence: up to 88 recipes move or hold, and pasta alone needs five or six new commodities with captures before 42 recipes can stay live.
